outcome: Classification of congenital uterine anomalies (arcuate, septate, bicornuate, unicornuate, didelphys)
cohort: The study included 950 women who underwent lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) for various obstetric indications.
finding: The prevalence of congenital uterine anomalies detected during caesarean section was 3.5%, with arcuate uterus being the most common type, and these anomalies were more common in primigravida women and those with malpresentation, intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), or previous first-trimester loss.
cross-section timing: Over a 15-month period from October 2023 to December 2024
